challenge.back_up: proceed, revised: the how is narrowed to the traceback source echo, keeping 'Captured stdout' sections readable, per the hidden assumption.
challenge.better_approach: Considered anchoring on pytest's echo shape instead (source lines in a traceback are prefixed by the function's indent, and the failing line by '>'), but docstring lines carry no prefix, so the section boundary is the only shape that separates them. Considered requiring a test_ identifier for every label tooth, which would break the 17 label-only proofs 9ac5f5e882f1's history names. The section skip is the smallest change.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That no proof prints its per-tooth report lines after pytest's FAILURES rule. pytest prints captured stdout of a failing test inside that section ('Captured stdout call'), so a proof's own ok/red lines may sit there: the fix must keep reading 'Captured stdout' blocks and skip only the traceback source echo. That is the measurement the build must take first over the sealed corpus.
challenge.prior_art: Consulted commons tickets naming teeth_printed/_MARKER_LABEL: 8e2018855b31 (PROVED, a green proof's data row mints no red), 8f5ab45e64c5 (a path label is data), 9ac5f5e882f1 (PROVEME:waiting, only report words mint label teeth) and d845546b67b9 (NOTRUN markers). All four govern lines a proof itself prints; none governs pytest's own traceback echo, and 9ac5 keeps 'green' a report word, so this line still mints. Distinction, not prior art.
challenge.real_collision: 9ac5f5e882f1 edits the same function and is at PROVEME; this is a distinction (different lines), but the two builds touch teeth_printed, so this one lands after 9ac5 to avoid a stale seal on 9ac5's proof.

answers.falsifier: Done when a red proof's stdout whose pytest traceback echoes an indented 'green ...' docstring line seals no tooth named by that line, and an indented 'ok <name>' report line printed before the FAILURES rule still reads green. Wrong intent if proofs legitimately print per-tooth report lines inside the FAILURES section (then the fix must anchor on the echo's shape, not the section).
answers.from_idea: none, because it is a defect measured at its site, cairn/tools/proof_coverage/proof_coverage.py:103 (_MARKER_LABEL), on 09f5cc38e16f's red-first seal (cairn/devices/tester/validations/test_the_hollow_reads_a_tooth_this_host_cannot_run_as_unread.json at a071e6b10, entry 0)
answers.how: teeth_printed skips the lines inside pytest's failure section (from the '= FAILURES =' rule to the '= short test summary info =' rule, or the end) before any label pattern reads them; a red-first proof feeds teeth_printed a stdout whose traceback echoes an indented docstring line opening 'green for the wrong reason.' and asserts no tooth is minted from it, while a genuine indented report line outside that section still reads.
answers.traces_to: Law 8 (nothing enters proven-space without a proof a hollow build couldn't pass: a tooth name minted from echoed source is coverage evidence nobody earned) and Law 3 (the seal's teeth are a measurement and must record only what was measured)
answers.what: proof_coverage's tooth parser never mints a tooth from a line pytest echoes as source inside a failure traceback, so a red proof's printed docstring can never add a green tooth to its seal.

bullets.text: A red proof's pytest traceback echoes the failing function's source, docstring included; proof_coverage read one indented docstring line opening 'green for the wrong reason.' as a green tooth on 09f5's red-first seal. It cannot green a declared tooth, but it puts an unearned name in teeth_green.
